quick_notes.title: Thirukkural Master Table (Recap)
quick_notes.detail: Aram (38), Porul (70), Inbam (25). Total 133 Adhikarams. English : G.U. Pope, Latin: Beschi. Names : Muppaal, Ulaga Podhumarai.
quick_notes.explanation: Thirukkural is an ancient Tamil text about how to live a good life. It is divided into three major parts, called Muppaal, which means "three divisions." These divisions are Aram (which means virtue or righteousness, like doing good deeds), Porul (which means wealth or politics, like how to manage society and money), and Inbam (which means love or pleasure, like family happiness). The entire book has 133 chapters, called Adhikarams, with Aram containing 38 chapters, Porul containing 70 chapters, and Inbam containing 25 chapters. It is also called Ulaga Podhumarai, which means "universal common scripture" because its lessons apply to everyone. The most famous English translation was done by G.U. Pope, and the first Latin translation was done by a missionary named Beschi. So, the table shows that the book has 133 total Adhikarams split across three parts: Aram (38), Porul (70), Inbam (25), and is known by the names Muppaal and Ulaga Podhumarai.

quick_notes.title: Ettuthokai & Pattuppattu Recap
quick_notes.detail: Ettuthokai (8): Purananuru (War), Akananuru (Love), Pathitrupathu (Cheras). Pattuppattu (10): Mullaippaattu (Shortest), Maduraikanchi (Longest).
quick_notes.explanation: Ettuthokai and Pattuppattu are two collections of ancient Tamil poems from the Sangam period. Ettuthokai means "eight anthologies" and includes eight books, such as Purananuru which is about war and heroism, Akananuru which is about love, and Pathitrupathu which praises the Che

quick_notes.title: The 5 Great Epics (Recap)
quick_notes.detail: Silappatikaram (Ilango), Manimekalai (Sathanar), Civaka Cintamani (Thirutthakka Devar). Silappatikaram : First Epic of Commoners.
quick_notes.explanation: Three of the Five Great Epics of Tamil literature are Silappatikaram, Manimekalai, and Civaka Cintamani. An epic is a long poem that tells the story of a hero or an important event. Silappatikaram, written by Ilango, is called the first epic of commoners because it focuses on the lives of ordinary people like Kannagi and Kovalan rather than kings or gods. Manimekalai was written by Sathanar, and Civaka Cintamani was written by Thirutthakka Devar. These three works are famous old Tamil poems.

quick_notes.title: Bhakti & Medieval Recap
quick_notes.detail: Nayanmars (63) - Periya Puranam. Alvars (12) - Divya Prabandham. Kamba Ramayanam (Ramavataram).
quick_notes.explanation: The Bhakti movement was a religious and social movement in medieval India that emphasized personal devotion to a god. The Nayanmars were 63 poet-saints from South India who were devoted to the Hindu god Shiva, and their life stories are collected in a Tamil text called the Periya Puranam. The Alvars were 12 poet-saints who were devoted to the Hindu god Vishnu, and their hymns are collected in a Tamil text called the Divya Prabandham. Another important Tamil work from this period is the Kamba Ramayanam, also known as Ramavataram, which is a retelling of the Sanskrit epic Ramayana by the poet Kamban. These texts and saints helped spread Bhakti ideas through simple, emotional poetry that people could sing and understand.

quick_notes.title: Modern Poets Recap
quick_notes.detail: Bharathiyar (Mahakavi, India magazine). Bharathidasan (Pavendar, Puratchikavi). Namakkal Kavignar (State Poet). Kavimani (Asia Jothi).
quick_notes.explanation: Bharathiyar, whose full name was Subramania Bharati, was a great poet, and he was known as Mahakavi, which means Great Poet in Tamil. He worked for a magazine called India, where he wrote about freedom and social reform. Bharathidasan, whose original name was Kanagasabai Subbu, was called Pavendar, meaning Poet of the People, and also Puratchikavi, meaning Revolutionary Poet, because his poems focused on social change and equality. Namakkal Kavignar, whose real name was V. Ramalingam Pillai, was honored as the State Poet of Tamil Nadu for his patriotic and simple verses. Kavimani, whose full name was V. S. Alagirisami, was known as the Asia Jothi, or Light of Asia, and his poems often dealt with nature and moral lessons.

lesson_intro: Today we celebrate the journey of the Tamil language. In TNPSC, the 'Literature' section is about precision—knowing exactly who wrote which epic and which poet edited which magazine. Today is for 'Author-Book Calibration'. Let's lock in the literature marks before we move to Geography and Administration.
